hook_text: Half a term of hydraulics fits in three facts and one three-step sum. Here they are before the exam.
clip_script: Fact one: gases squash, liquids do not. Spongy brakes, oil in jacks, done. Fact two: pressure in a trapped liquid is the same everywhere, so force over area is equal both sides, and a bigger area carries a bigger force. Fact three: the volume moved is the same both sides, so the big piston moves less; force up, distance down, work the same. The sum: pressure from the known side, apply it to the other side, check that the big area has the big force. 100 newtons on 5 gives 20; 20 on 50 gives 1000. The jack is that sum with a pump handle and valves. The systems diagram is boxes and arrows, not a picture.
visual_style: Whiteboard with three numbered facts appearing; two cylinders with equal pressure labels; a volume block moving from small to large; the three-step sum written out; a three-block systems diagram.
mood: Calm revision, like a friend going over notes the night before.
pacing: Fact, fact, fact, sum, example, jack, diagram.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and do the press sum with areas of 4 and 60 and a push of 50 newtons.
